Subject: Re: PrivGPU concurrency lane simulation - kickoff

Thanks for sending the initial scope, Dylan. Quick recap from our side: DataCore is trying to validate two things before we sign the carveout contract — (1) how the lane-based concurrency allocation behaves under mixed-request tail load (short chat requests interleaved with long completion jobs), and (2) the egress shaping impact on throughput when we hit NAT limits in our colo.

We ran a small smoke last week and saw a ~15% drop in short-request P50 when long jobs were concurrent on the same pod. We're hoping Redwood's tiling/provision plan can provide predictable degradation curves rather than the binary failure modes we've experienced with our current stack.

Can we schedule an engineering-led simulation this week? We can provide traffic traces and a sample ingress NAT config. Also attaching a short CSV with our observed request mix (lane_sim_input.csv).

Tom
Principal SRE, DataCore Solutions

Subject: Re: PrivGPU concurrency lane simulation - kickoff

Tom — thanks, this is helpful. Laura and Jonas + I reviewed the CSV and sketched an initial simulation plan. High level:

- Run three lane allocation profiles: (A) fixed equal lanes, (B) weighted lanes (short-heavy), (C) dynamic lane reclaim with cap on reclaim frequency.
- Inject mixed tails using your trace; include two long-job classes (L1: 30s average, L2: 90s average).
- Model NAT egress caps at 1Gbps and 500Mbps to see queuing at the pod egress.
- Collect: per-lane P50/P95 latency, KV cache hit rate, per-pod token throughput, and egress wait time.

Deliverables: consolidated CSV of sim runs, a simple cost delta based on additional reserved slots, and a diagram of tiling/host affinity. We'll throw our current sim output (lane_sim_v2.csv) and an egress cost worksheet in the shared folder after the run.

Propose Wed 26 May 2pm PT for the simulation session. Do you want to include a brief zoom to walk through the traces?

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior PM, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrivGPU concurrency lane simulation - kickoff

Following the run yesterday, I pushed the consolidated sim CSV and the egress-cost model to the shared Drive. Summary (high level):

- Profile A (equal lanes): predictable P95 for long jobs but short-job P50 suffers up to 25% at 500Mbps egress caps.
- Profile B (weighted lanes): short-job P50 improves (10-12%) at the expense of long-job tail (P95 worsens ~8%).
- Profile C (dynamic reclaim): best overall 95/50 balance if reclaim throttle is set to >= 15s; aggressive reclaiming creates instability.

Capacity translation notes for procurement (mapping QPS -> reserved GPU-hours):
- 1k steady short-request QPS (avg tokens 30) -> ~4 reserved A100-equivalent hours sustained per minute (approx 2.6 GPUs steady per region after multiplexing).
- Mixed 1k QPS with 10% long-job load (avg tokens 600) -> reserve ~3x the short-only allocation to avoid P95 degradation unless dynamic reclaim is enabled with conservative thresholds.

Operational recommendations:
- Set a soft egress shaper at the host-level to prioritize short lanes (TCP pacing + token-bucket, 5% burst allowance).
- Pin critical tenants to dedicated tiling lanes if they require sub-200ms P50.
- Include a regression test in the onboarding checklist that runs the dynamic reclaim profile against a canned trace.

I've attached the sim CSV (lane_sim_v2.csv) and the egress-cost model (egress-cost-model.xlsx) to the Drive link. Jon, can you add an ops note about NAT backend tuning?

Laura
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: PrivGPU concurrency lane simulation - kickoff

Quick follow-up and concrete next steps from ops side:

- I'll open a runbook PR (privgpu/ops/runbooks) with the recommended host-level shaper configs and a short checklist for pinning tenants.
- Action item for DataCore: share the NAT table and a sample egress ACL; we'll run an internal validation of the suggested 500Mbps shaping to confirm no packet drops under the simulated mix.
- Action item for Redwood product: include the GPU-hour mapping table (Laura's bullets) in the SOW appendix; procurement needs it for commit thresholds.

Decision: we will provision a conservative initial carveout for DataCore at 3x short-only allocation if they want minimal P95 impact without dynamic reclaim enabled. With dynamic reclaim (throttle >=15s) we can reduce that to ~1.6x with monitoring + auto-fallback.

Jonas
Engineering Lead, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
